name: AFS-KEX
full_name: Authenticated Forward-Secure Key Exchange: pMAKE-BW and pUAKE-BW

protocol.label_en: KEM-based mutually authenticated key exchange (primary pMAKE-BW profile)

authentication.mechanism: Primary pMAKE-BW authenticates both parties by reconstructing each certified static BW-KEM public key from a session-specific combined key and an XOR-protected ephemeral seed, followed by CA verification; no online digital signature is used.

roles.key_details: Holds a certified static BW-KEM key pair and creates fresh seed_A, ephemeral key material, and a combined key cpk_A/csk_A.
Holds a certified static BW-KEM key pair and creates fresh seed_B, ephemeral key material, and a combined key cpk_B/csk_B.

pre_distributed_material: CA trust anchor or equivalent authenticated public directory
NGCC evaluation profile pre-provides each peer's static and combined public keys before the online four-pass exchange

forward_secrecy.conditions: Claimed in the post-eCK-PFS model for fresh completed sessions; later static-key compromise alone must not be combined with disallowed session-key or relevant ephemeral-state exposure.

protocol_characteristics.key_confirmation: Explicit authentication and key confirmation are claimed. In the NGCC implementation, pass 4 carries no payload and completes responder-side verification/confirmation.
protocol_characteristics.transcript_binding: The generic pMAKE session key derives from both AFS-KEM secrets and the protocol's certified-identity/public-key reconstruction; the security definition matches the KEM-related transcript (cpk_A, cpk_B, ct_A, ct_B). The implementation KDF consumes K_B || K_A after the interface has bound the supplied public keys and protected seeds.
protocol_characteristics.identity_binding: Each recovered static public key is checked against the claimed identity through CAVerf; the generic protocol sends identities during the handshake, whereas the NGCC profile assumes peer static/combined public keys are already supplied.

technical_classification.construction_paradigm: Signature-free post-specified-identity AKE built from an authenticated forward-secure KEM; the primary pMAKE composes two AFS-KEM contributions, while pUAKE uses one.

underlying_primitives.name: AFS-KEM-BW

components.name: ct_B
components.semantics: BW-KEM ciphertext encapsulated to responder combined public key cpk_B.

protocol_flow.semantics: NGCC evaluated profile pass 1. The generic post-ID pMAKE specification instead sends cpk_A in round 1.

components.name: ct_A
components.semantics: BW-KEM ciphertext encapsulated to initiator combined public key cpk_A.

components.name: c_seed_B
components.semantics: XOR protection K_ENC^B XOR seed_B used by the initiator to reconstruct and verify responder static key material.

protocol_flow.semantics: NGCC evaluated profile pass 2; responder derives K_A and decapsulates ct_B to obtain K_B.

components.name: c_seed_A
components.semantics: XOR protection K_ENC^A XOR seed_A used by the responder to reconstruct and verify initiator static key material.

protocol_flow.semantics: Initiator decapsulates ct_A, derives the session and seed-protection keys, verifies responder key binding, and returns protected seed_A.

Zero-byte final pass in the NGCC implementation: responder reconstructs the initiator ephemeral key, extracts and verifies the static public key, and completes key confirmation. The generic pMAKE specification represents the final responder-to-initiator identity/protected-seed message explicitly.

static_contributions: Certified static BW-KEM key components sk_A/pk_A and sk_B/pk_B are included in combined keys csk_U = sk_U + sk_Ue and cpk_U = pk_U + pk_Ue.
ephemeral_contributions: Fresh seed_A and seed_B deterministically generate ephemeral BW-KEM key components for each session.
K_A and K_B are the two BW-KEM shared secrets encapsulated to cpk_A and cpk_B.
key_schedule.transcript_hash: No separate transcript-hash formula is specified for the NGCC implementation; the formal analysis binds the KEM transcript (cpk_A, cpk_B, ct_A, ct_B) through the AFS-KEM construction and identity/key reconstruction.
key_schedule.session_key_derivation: (K_SESSION, K_AENC, K_BENC) = PRF(K_A, K_B); implementation applies the configured XOF to the concatenation K_B || K_A and emits three security-parameter-length strings.
key_schedule.domain_separation: BW-KEM random-oracle inputs use deterministic public-key identifiers ID(pk); no distinct textual AKE domain-separation label was found.
key_schedule.ephemeral_secret_erasure: The security model assumes all protocol randomness/ephemeral state is securely erased when a session accepts or rejects; encapsulation randomness is erased after computation.

correctness.relationship: Primary pMAKE-BW performs two correctness-relevant AFS-KEM decapsulations, so the honest-session failure probability is at most 2*delta_AFS by a union bound.
correctness.basis: Specification Table 1 (p.17) and the two-AFS-KEM pMAKE flow (pp.10-11); session bounds are derived, not separately tabulated by the submitter.

security_claims.claim: Primary pMAKE-BW provides mutual explicit authentication and match soundness; secondary pUAKE-BW provides unilateral initiator authentication.
Key secrecy is proved in the post-eCK-PFS model in both ROM and QROM.
security_claims.comparison_scope: Subject to the stated freshness predicate and primitive assumptions

security_claims.claim: Completed fresh sessions retain key secrecy after later long-term-key compromise.
The proof uses AFS-KEM IND-ECPA, IND-SCCA and IND-LCK-SCCA properties reduced to MLWE through AFS-PKE-BW and FO_AFS.
pMAKE-BW claims secrecy as long as at least one of four static/ephemeral secret sources remains unexposed in the relevant matched-session cases.
security_claims.comparison_scope: Formal freshness cases described for pMAKE

claimed_advantages.claim: The pMAKE-BW structure uses two standard KEM public keys, two standard KEM ciphertexts and two short protected seeds in the generic post-ID accounting, reducing the dominant KEM material relative to direct parallel-KEM baselines.
claimed_advantages.comparison_scope: Table 4 KEM-based AKE baselines; identity lengths omitted

claimed_advantages.claim: Provides PFS, explicit authentication, match soundness, and stronger resistance to reusable-key decryption-failure amplification.
claimed_advantages.comparison_scope: post-eCK-PFS model and discussed DFA setting

claimed_advantages.claim: Online authentication is signature-free and reuses native BW-KEM encapsulation/decapsulation code.
AVX2 performance implementation accelerates a complete exchange by about 4.2x-6.3x over the portable reference implementation.
claimed_advantages.comparison_scope: Single Intel Xeon Platinum 8575C test platform

claimed_advantages.claim: The generic AFS-KEM interface is described as compatible with suitable MLWE, LWE, and code-based KEM public-key structures.
claimed_advantages.comparison_scope: Generic framework; submitted concrete suite uses BW-KEM

limitations_and_constraints.description: Authentication requires a CA/PKI or authenticated public directory binding identities to static public keys.
The NGCC implementation pre-provides peer static and combined public keys and omits identity/certificate bytes from online communication; this differs from the generic post-ID message syntax.
Composite-key AFS-KEM has nonzero decryption failure; the base submitted instances range from about 2^-67.98 to 2^-124.13 per AFS-KEM operation.
Identity hiding is not a property of the base protocol and requires an optional CRS/common-matrix profile plus encrypted credential transmission.
The claimed proofs model PRF/PRG and relevant hashes in ROM/QROM.
Ephemeral randomness must be erased at completion, and offline retention of precomputed encapsulated keys should be avoided because it can enable a KCI-style state-leakage attack.
x86 benchmarks use one Xeon Platinum 8575C/Ubuntu 22.04 system; Cortex-M4 results use STM32F4DISCOVERY and 1,000 repetitions.

review_notes: Each NGCC total was recomputed as m1+m2+m3+m4: 1568, 2944 and 6016 bytes.
Parameter and failure values were checked against Table 1; interface sizes and pass semantics were checked against implementation getters/comments.
Primary pMAKE-BW and secondary pUAKE-BW were kept distinct; the top-level classification and sizes follow the evaluated primary pMAKE-BW profile.
Independent cross-review by group_3 corrected long-term key sizes to the composite NGCC interface values in Table 6 and kex_get_*_len_bytes().
conflicts: The generic pMAKE description sends combined keys and identities in four messages, while the NGCC evaluation profile assumes key material is pre-supplied and reports only two ciphertexts plus two protected seeds online.
The title-page author list includes Jian Weng, but the basic-information submitter table does not; his affiliation is left unresolved.

Long-term key sizes use the doubled NGCC interface buffers (combined key plus certified static key), as reported by Table 6 and the kex_get_pk/sk_len_bytes getters; underlying single BW-KEM object sizes remain in core_parameters.
Top-level flow follows the byte-accounted NGCC evaluated profile; generic post-ID pMAKE message differences are explicitly documented in flow semantics and review conflicts.
